EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows an aromatic molecule with both aromatic (3065 cm⁻¹) and aliphatic (2922 cm⁻¹) C–H stretches, indicating an alkyl-substituted aryl ring.  

Key diagnostic bands:  
• 718 cm⁻¹ (very strong) – typical aryl C–Cl stretch / C–H out-of-plane bend for chloro-substituted benzenes, consistent with a ring-bound Cl atom in candidate 2.  
• 997 cm⁻¹ (very strong) – benzene A₁g ring-breathing mode of a monosubstituted/para-disubstituted ring, present in chloro- and thioanisole derivatives.  
• 1095 cm⁻¹ (medium) – strong C–O stretch of an aryl methoxy (O–CH₃) group, present only in candidate 2 and 5; candidate 5 lacks aromatic bands.  
• 1264/1277 cm⁻¹ and 1374/1439 cm⁻¹ – CH₃ rocking and deformation modes of a methoxy methyl; candidate 2 contains such a group.  
• 541–557 cm⁻¹ (medium) – C–S stretching region, matching the thioether (S–aryl) bond in candidate 2.  
• 1580/1596 cm⁻¹ – aromatic C=C stretches, required by an aryl ring.  

Among the candidates, only 2 (COCSc1ccc(Cl)cc1) possesses all of the functional groups implied by the observed bands: an aromatic ring, a methoxy group (O–CH₃), a thioether C–S bond, and an aryl C–Cl bond, each with matching Raman features. Therefore it is the most consistent choice.
